conceptZh: 「水」字化成四筆清楚的藍色小水道，紙船順著中央豎鉤漂流，在鉤尾輕輕轉彎。
object: A cobalt-blue watercourse shaped precisely like 水, with one tiny yellow paper boat.
morph: Begin with the complete glyph. Water moves inside its four fixed stroke silhouettes; the central vertical hook carries a tiny boat, while the three surrounding strokes remain separate, clearly defined channels. Surface details gradually disappear into a solid blue glyph.
creativeAngle: 從完整字形出發，把中央豎鉤變成紙船的轉彎水道；用小船轉向的驚喜凸顯鉤筆，避免水花變字造成筆畫模糊。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second animation teaching the Traditional Chinese character 水 to a Taiwanese child aged 6–8. Use a locked, straight-on overhead view against a warm, pale cream background. From the first frame, show one correctly formed 水, centered and uncropped, approximately 70% of frame height with generous margins. Base its exact four-stroke silhouette on a standard Traditional Chinese educational typeface. Render those strokes as saturated cobalt-blue enamel water channels with shallow water inside; preserve every stroke boundary and the open spaces between strokes throughout.

At 0.6 seconds, a tiny yellow paper boat appears within the top of the central vertical stroke. It drifts downward, making the meaning of water tangible. Restrained ripples travel separately along the left bent stroke, upper-right short falling stroke, and lower-right sweeping stroke, without connecting their channels or extending beyond their silhouettes. At 2.8 seconds, the boat reaches the central hook: the current gently turns its pointed bow along the hook, giving it a charming little change of direction. Keep the boat small enough that the blue stroke remains clearly readable around it. By 4.2 seconds, dissolve the boat and internal ripples while smoothly flattening the enamel shading. From 4.2 through 8.0 seconds, hold the resulting solid cobalt-blue 水 completely still and unobstructed for 3.8 full seconds.

A warm adult voice clearly pronounces 水 four times in Taiwanese Mandarin, shuǐ, ㄕㄨㄟˇ, with a natural isolated third tone, beginning at 0.2, 2.1, 4.6, and 6.6 seconds. Use soft water sounds beneath the action, quiet during speech and silent during the final hold. The watercourse is a playful visual metaphor, not an explanation of historical etymology. Keep the composition bright but not neon, with no camera movement, flashing effects, additional writing, subtitles, logos, watermarks, or background props.

conceptZh: 靜止的溫暖乳白瓷盤上方，竹管湧出清澈藍色泉水，順流而下形成「水」字中央豎鉤，再往兩旁分流填滿左右三筆，最後凝結成清晰穩定的鈷藍色標準正體「水」字。
object: A miniature bamboo spring spout dispensing clear aqua water onto a pale cream porcelain surface.
morph: The main stream flows downward to carve the central hooked vertical stroke, while branching streamlets fill the left angled stroke and right falling/sweeping strokes of the glyph.
creativeAngle: 區隔於前一版的紙船漂流設計，改採用竹管泉水自然湧流與動態分流的實體物理隱喻。藉由中央主水流與兩側分支水流精準勾勒出「水」字的四個筆畫，並在流動完成後迅速凝固為飽和的鈷藍色字體，達成筆順清晰度與長達3.2秒的穩定定格。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animation teaching the Traditional Chinese character 水 to a Taiwanese child aged 6–8. Use a locked, straight-on overhead camera angle against a warm, pale cream porcelain background. Centered in the frame, a smooth miniature bamboo spout positioned at the top center releases a sparkling stream of translucent aqua-blue spring water. At 0.4 seconds, the main water stream glides vertically downward, curving gently at the bottom to form the central hooked vertical stroke (豎鉤). At 1.8 seconds, two smaller trickles branch out from the main stream: one glides to the left to form the angled stroke (橫撇), while the other flows right, splitting into the upper-right falling stroke (撇) and lower-right sweeping stroke (捺). The water streams fill the precise four-stroke silhouette of a standard Traditional Chinese educational typeface for 水, maintaining distinct stroke boundaries without spilling over. At 3.6 seconds, the bamboo spout smoothly retracts upward out of frame while the flowing water inside the four strokes instantly settles into a solid, vibrant cobalt-blue enamel glyph. From 4.8 seconds to 8.0 seconds, hold the completed, solid blue 水 character completely still and unobstructed for a full 3.2-second final hold, occupying approximately 70% of the frame height with clean margins. A warm adult voice clearly pronounces 水 four times in Taiwanese Mandarin, shuǐ, ㄕㄨㄟˇ, with a natural isolated third tone, at 0.2, 2.0, 4.6, and 6.6 seconds. Soft, relaxing water trickling sounds accompany the liquid animation, turning silent during the final hold. Keep the lighting bright and warm, with zero camera motion, flashing effects, subtitles, extra text, logos, or watermarks.

conceptZh: 把「水」字變成淺淺的藍色水池。愛彈跳的扭蛋小怪獸以為水面也能彈，跳下去卻變成一小團濕毛球，最後改用仰漂，得意地游走。
object: A cobalt-blue, glyph-shaped shallow pool and an original fuzzy pocket creature toy in a gachapon capsule.
morph: The correctly formed 水 remains fixed throughout. Brief ripples stay inside its four-stroke silhouette; the surface settles into a uniform solid-blue glyph for the final hold.
creativeAngle: 不再用水流拼字，而讓完整字形直接示範水的特性：小怪獸把水面當彈床，蓬鬆大毛球落水後縮成小濕球，尺寸反差形成笑點；最後學會仰漂，保留清楚字形與充足定格。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation with a locked overhead camera and a warm pale-apricot background. From the first frame, show one correctly formed Traditional Chinese 水, centered, uncropped, and occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use the exact four-stroke outline of a standard Taiwanese educational typeface, including the central vertical hook and clearly separated surrounding negative spaces. Render this silhouette as a shallow cobalt-blue pool without an added border. Its saturated outline remains stationary and readable throughout.

The lead is an original round, fuzzy coral pocket creature toy: tiny stubby limbs, oversized expressive eyes, and wildly overconfident bouncing energy. Its only supporting prop is a small unmarked gachapon capsule, initially in the lower-right margin outside the glyph. At 0.25 seconds, the capsule pops open softly and the creature springs out, rebounds once off the capsule, then once off the dry floor. The capsule halves tumble out of frame together. By 1.5 seconds, the creature has noticed the broad lower-right sweeping stroke of 水. It crouches eagerly, pauses in anticipation, and launches toward the blue surface, confidently tucking itself into a bouncing ball.

At 2.3 seconds, the expected rebound becomes a soft plop: it sinks briefly into the shallow water instead. A small ripple stays entirely inside the stroke. At 2.7 seconds, it resurfaces safely, its enormous fluffy coat flattened into a hilariously tiny wet sphere with the same oversized eyes. Hold its bewildered blink for a beat. Then its expression brightens: it rolls onto its back, floats successfully, and paddles smugly along the lower-right stroke toward its outer tip. Keep the creature small relative to the glyph and away from the central stroke junction. It climbs onto the dry background and makes two little soggy hops out of frame by 4.7 seconds. Any tiny droplets disappear with it; the pool silhouette never stretches or gains extra marks.

From 4.7 to 8.0 seconds, hold the single finished 水 completely still and unobstructed for 3.3 seconds. Settle all internal ripples and shading into an even, saturated cobalt-blue fill against the light background.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly「水、水、水池」. Place the first 水 around 0.45 seconds, the second around 1.35 seconds, and 水池 around 5.4 seconds, with natural pauses and an unhurried delivery. Stop after 水池. Use quiet toy boings and one gentle water plop beneath the voice; no music. The vocabulary is audio only. All visible figures and objects are original stylized animated toys. Keep only the single target glyph on screen, with no subtitles, other writing, logos, watermark, clutter, camera movement, or flashing effects.
